title: Evidence Trace and SIEM Handoff Procedure
content:
Purpose:
This runbook standardizes how we collect, verify, and hand off digital evidence from Redwood systems into the SIEM and forensic teams. It focuses on fast triage, minimal attacker disturbance, preserving chain of custody, and mapping exported artifacts to the audit-log schema (v2).

Scope and when to use it:
- Use for suspected compromise, data-exfiltration indicators, suspicious admin activity, or when SIEM needs raw artifacts for investigation.
- Not for full forensic imaging of physical devices; see forensics team for host-takeover workflows.

Primary objectives:
1) Capture the minimum set of artifacts that preserve investigatory value and audit trails.
2) Export SIEM queries and raw logs in a verifiable format.
3) Document RBAC escalations and temporary access grants used during collection.
4) Transfer artifacts to evidence storage with verifiable hashes and access logs.

Roles and responsibilities:
- Incident Commander (IC): owns decision to invoke this runbook and approves evidence storage location.
- Evidence Collector (EC): executes collection steps (SIEM exports, API log pulls, config snapshots).
- Forensics Lead: advises on deep-dive needs (disk images, memory dumps).
- Platform SRE: assists with privileged exports and temporary RBAC tweaks.
- Legal/Compliance: consulted for sensitive data handling and preservation holds.

Prerequisites and access requirements:
- Evidence Collector must have an assigned security role: security:evidence-collector (ephemeral).
- Platform SRE or IAM engineer must be on-call to create ephemeral role if not present.
- Destination evidence bucket (s3://redwood-evidence-prod or GCS equivalent) preconfigured with KMS key and audit logging.
- GPG key for signing artifacts or organization HSM available.

RBAC and audit considerations:
- Prefer using an ephemeral role with time-limited policy rather than escalating existing admin accounts.
- Before granting, record the following in the incident ticket: who, why, scope, start_time, expected_end_time.
- On role grant completion, capture the RBAC grant event (IAM audit log) and include it in the artifact bundle.

Minimum evidence checklist (first 60 minutes):
- SIEM search artifact(s): export queries and results for the time window (UTC) and include query DSL or search string.
- API gateway logs for implicated services (request_id, client_ip, user_agent, latency).
- Authentication/audit logs: successful/failed logins, token creations, role assumption events.
- Orchestration events: deploys, config changes, canary switches within the time window.
- Networking telemetry: VPC flow logs, top talkers, connection count spikes.
- Container/host runtime logs: stdout/stderr for implicated containers, process lists if live access allowed.
- Snapshot of relevant infra state: instance metadata, container images (sha), config files.

Evidence capture procedure (high level):
1) Confirm time window of interest with IC and forensic lead. Use UTC and include drifts.
2) Freeze the query: copy the query string, timestamp, and parameters into the incident ticket.
3) Export SIEM results to an artifact file (CSV/NDJSON) and store in a temporary evidence workspace.
4) Collect associated raw logs (source system) matching the search window and save as compressed files.
5) For each exported file compute SHA256 and sign if possible.
6) Push artifacts to the approved evidence bucket and set object ACLs to readonly for evidence-role only.
7) Update the incident ticket with locations, checksums, and RBAC events.

SIEM export primitives (examples):
- Splunk (UI): run search, use Export > JSON/CSV. For automation: use /services/search/jobs/export with auth token.
  Example curl (token masked):
  curl -k -u ":$SPLUNK_TOKEN" https://splunk.internal/api/search/jobs/export -d search='search index=prod_logs "unexpected auth"' -d output_mode=json > splunk_export_20251012.json

- Elastic (Elasticsearch): use _search with scroll for large result sets.
  Example curl:
  curl -s -u user:pass -H "Content-Type: application/json" -X POST "https://es.internal/_search?scroll=1m" -d '{"query": {"match": {"message": "failed token"}}, "size":1000}' > es_export_page1.json

- Datadog: use Logs API to pull by query and time window, then write to file.

- Cloud Provider Logging (GCP/AWS): prefer export sink to GCS/S3 for large ranges; otherwise use gcloud/aws CLI filtered reads.
  GCP example:
  gcloud logging read 'resource.type="k8s_cluster" AND textPayload: "token"' --limit 1000 --format json > gcp_logs.json
  AWS example (CloudWatch):
  aws logs filter-log-events --log-group-name /aws/whatever --start-time 1697040000000 --end-time 1697126400000 --filter-pattern 'ERROR' > cw_logs.json

Mapping exports to audit-log schema v2 (quick reference):
- source_timestamp -> event_time (ISO8601 UTC)
- request_id / trace_id -> event_trace_id
- principal (user/service) -> actor_id
- action -> event_action (canonicalized: e.g., auth.login, token.create, deploy.apply)
- resource -> event_resource (resource_type:id)
- ip -> source_ip
- outcome -> event_outcome (success|failure|unknown)
- raw_payload -> original_payload (store as NDJSON file)

Include a small manifest file with each evidence bundle named manifest.txt with fields: bundle_id, collected_by, ic, start_utc, end_utc, query_strings (attach), checksums (sha256 list), destination_object_uris, rbacs_granted (yes/no + link to IAM audit).

Chain of custody and verification (required):
1) After writing artifact to local workspace, compute sha256sum and create artifact.sig (GPG) or HSM-signed checksum.
   Example: sha256sum splunk_export_20251012.json > splunk_export_20251012.json.sha256
   gpg --default-key "secops@redwood.ai" --detach-sign splunk_export_20251012.json
2) Upload file, checksum, and signature to evidence bucket under folder incidents/IR-####/raw/.
3) Enable object lock (if available) or set retention policy as per IC instruction.
4) Capture bucket write event log and include the storage write event as evidence.

Post-handoff verification and handover notes to forensics:
- Confirm forensics can open NDJSON/CSV and that checksums validate. Provide the manifest and the RBAC audit entries.
- If forensic imaging is later requested, note that live logs were already exported and should not be overwritten.

Temporary RBAC creation template (example):
- policy: Allow read only on logs, assume role session duration 3600s, require mfa.
- request body in ticket: who, reason, scope (log groups, indices), start, end.
- revoke: EC must close the role and capture revoke event.

Escalation and communications:
- If evidence contains PII or regulated data, notify Legal within 30 minutes.
- If evidence export fails due to permission errors, escalate to Platform SRE with tag @oncall-iam.
- All external sharing requires Legal approval and secure SCP transfer to partner SIEM.

Retention and audit after incident closure:
- Evidence bundles retained according to retention policy attached to IR ticket. Default: 1 year for security incidents unless Legal instructs otherwise.
- Periodically (quarterly) run a verification job that validates checksums of stored incident bundles and logs results in the SOC audit dashboard.

Appendix A — Example minimal manifest.txt (plain text):
- bundle_id: IR-4123-bundle-20251012
- collected_by: Maya Chen
- ic: Connor Lee
- start_utc: 2025-10-12T14:00:00Z
- end_utc: 2025-10-12T15:30:00Z
- queries: splunk: "index=prod_logs user:unknown"; es: {"match": {"message":"token"}}
- files: splunk_export_20251012.json -> sha256: abc123...
- rbacs_granted: yes -> iam-event: projects/iam/events/12345

Appendix B — Quick troubleshooting notes:
- If Splunk export times out, reduce time window and export in slices.
- If ES scroll fails with 403, check role scope and request ephemeral role list for indices.
- If bucket upload fails with KMS error, capture KMS error log and escalate to Platform SRE (kms-oncall).

Notes and outstanding items (work in progress):
- Automate manifest generation with the ir-scripts repo (linked artifact) and add a GitHub Action to upload and sign artifacts.
- Add a lightweight UI in Console to request evidence role grants with built-in approval flow.

Contact list for emergency access:
- Platform IAM on-call: iam-ops@redwood.ai
- SRE on-call: sre-oncall@redwood.ai
- Security on-call: sec-oncall@redwood.ai

End of procedure.
